r_zvem3yg7jtxbsxbop3ypzy.desc: For the HAXcms site, all documentation is located in the `docs` folder. The site structure includes `site.json` for page order in JSON outline schema format, all files are under the `files` folder, and all page HTML content is in the `pages` folder. Documentation should ensure coverage of pillars, pedagogical ontology, and relevant projects referenced in AGENTS.md to maintain comprehensive ecosystem context. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: haxcms). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_rhq7llrzmzlnfvelrwslun.desc: In a site.json / hax site the metadata.site.name property is used to help establish the correct basePath in some scenarios. This value should not be modified to be anything other than put into alignment with the name of the folder the site is named. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: haxcms). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_q4d9hl9sfnorlmpt1z2zeb.desc: The `x/` prefix for routes is reserved for internal HAXcms paths such as `x/search` and `x/tags`. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: haxcms). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_69qeidwqwmafq9ewziwmln.desc: wc-registry.json is a file that is built by the ubiquity script and is used for our "magic script". This register contains references to every valid web component that we publish on our CDN and is hydrated based on tag-name being undefined, detected in the DOM, and then imported dynamically at the associated object key. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_tjnufvxe11bgtoleu8opxk.desc: For any git repository in the HAX ecosystem, check issues against the unified issue queue at https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues (for example `gh issue list --repo haxtheweb/issues`). In PRAW RULES.md (scope: global). Guidance by design: no check enforces this, and none is planned. Where to look for issues: a working habit, nothing a check could decide.

r_a8bf4a47_3d4f_4f8e_a356_a04db66ce1ab.desc: Anytime an audit or security issue is raised for either `haxcms-nodejs` or `haxcms-php`, verify and resolve it in both backends to maintain feature parity and security consistency. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: haxcms). Enforced by Backend parity, nightly. Nightly backend parity run (report only).

r_82dc87fd_6bc1_4d20_9d68_5b077bb88b89.desc: System-level calls (site imports, file format conversions, operations not scoped to a single site) must use the MicroFrontendRegistry (MFR) `@system/` namespace, registered from the on-premises OpenAPI spec at `/system/api/v1` (see `app-hax-system-api-registry.js` and `system-spec.yaml`; handlers in `haxcms-nodejs/src/systemRoutes/v1`). Site-scoped calls must use the `@site/` namespace (handlers in `haxcms-nodejs/src/siteRoutes/v1`); v0 site endpoints are removed. Do not add new `@haxcms/`-namespaced registrations or route new work through the retired `open-apis` broker (the legacy v0 import path) — use `@system/` or `@site/` instead. A new site importer is complete only when every layer is wired and each repo has its PR open without being asked: both backends (`haxcms-nodejs` and `haxcms-php`, same behavior), the webcomponents client (MFR service and chooser card), and the `create` CLI, where `IMPORT_STRUCTURE_MAP` must map `<name>ToSite` to the `site/import/:platform` dispatcher (which calls the v1 handlers in-process) and the name must be listed in `--import-structure` help, the man page and the README. Use the `hax-importer-dev` skill. (Full detail lives in `haxcms/WARP.md`.) In PRAW RULES.md (scope: haxcms). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_d513754d87c145d6a166ec.desc: Keep the two MobX stores separate. `HAXStore` (`hax-body/lib/hax-store.js`) owns editor state (active node, edit mode, gizmo, preferences, tour); `haxcms-site-store` (`haxcms-elements/lib/core/haxcms-site-store.js`) owns site/CMS state (manifest, active page/route, site metadata, theme configuration). `haxcms-site-editor-ui` is the only bridge between them and runs the save flow (editor content, then backend API, then manifest update). HAXStore must never know about CMS routing, and the site store must never manipulate page DOM content. Rationale and flow: KNOWLEDGE.md entry "Dual-store architecture". In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_1286150dc8944178aa82ca.desc: When changing API endpoints or auth code in haxcms-php or haxcms-nodejs, check the HAXiam path (`config->iam`) as well as single-tenant mode. In multi-tenant mode each user has an isolated sites directory, and endpoints such as `connectionSettings` must enforce strict alignment between the authenticated user and the requested path (for example `getIAMTenantUserName()` and `getRequestPathUserName()`). Never weaken that check, and verify the change in both backends. Rationale: KNOWLEDGE.md entry "HAXiam multi-tenant auth model". In PRAW RULES.md (scope: haxcms). Enforced by haxiam nightly. Partly. haxcms-nodejs and haxcms-php run a nightly HAXiam isolation job: throwaway multi-tenant users on localhost must not list, read, edit, clone or download each other's sites. A failure turns the run red and files an issue; it doesn't block a pull request.

r_54e36477_ac8a_4fb2_bd9e_c46463f608aa.desc: HAXcms never updates itself from the web process. The admin panel's Status page and the system status report only say that a release or a missing security fix exists (security status comes from the published advisories on haxtheweb/issues, matched by each backend's package name and patched version) and show the steps for the detected install method; they never download, unpack or write release files, and no endpoint may be added that does. Upgrades run from a shell as the user who owns the files: `php scripts/platform-upgrade.php upgrade|verify|rollback` for haxcms-php installs, which `hax platform upgrade|verify|rollback` runs for you; npm, Docker and git installs are updated with the tool they came from. The upgrader is driven by the release manifest (`platform-manifest.json`): it writes only manifest-listed code paths after checking the archive against `SHA256SUMS` and every file against the manifest, backs up what it changes, never touches `_config`, `_sites`, `_published` or `_archived`, and rolls back on a failed check. On a HAXiam (`haxiam-managed`) deployment the host manages HAXcms: no update checks run, and `upgrade`, `verify` and `rollback` refuse in both the PHP script and the CLI. Keep these invariants in any change to the status report, the upgrader, the CLI or the release workflow (haxtheweb/issues#1768). In PRAW RULES.md (scope: haxcms). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_7e2c1a94_3b58_4d0f_9c6a_1f8e4d2b5a30.desc: Never rename, move, or delete the canonical repository folders in the local HAX ecosystem working directory (the folder that holds all HAX repo checkouts — for example `create`, `webcomponents`, `haxcms-nodejs`, `haxcms-php`, `praw`, `docs`, `issues`). These folders are the single source of truth for local work; renaming a canonical folder (e.g. to a hidden `.name-<suffix>` copy) makes the work it contains effectively lost. If a repo must be duplicated for isolation (parallel agents, test fixtures), work in a hidden dot-suffixed copy (e.g. `.create-t0D9Xyd1`) and leave the canonical folder in place. When the work is finished, restore relocated checkouts to their canonical names. If a canonical folder is missing or gutted (only `node_modules` / lockfiles remain), recover it from the newest clean git checkout (including hidden copies and `.backup_*` folders) and put it back under its canonical name before doing further work there. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: global). Guidance by design: no check enforces this, and none is planned. About folders on the machine an agent works on, which no repository check can see.

r_9f3c2a7e_6b1d_4e8a_9c5f_2d7b8e1a4f60.desc: Five repos document HAX's core contracts/data-shapes; each is documentation-only (no runtime code) — the consuming runtime lives in `webcomponents`. Read the relevant one before authoring against, or asking an agent to reason about, that contract: `json-outline-schema` (`site.json`'s outline structure: `items` with `id`/`parent`/`order`/`indent`/`location`/`slug`, plus the Skeleton API for starter-site templates; consumed by both HAXcms backends and `haxcms-site-store`); `hax-schema` (`haxProperties`/HAXSchema — the contract that makes a web component HAX-capable: gizmo metadata, `settings` form fields, `haxHooks` lifecycle integration, `demoSchema`); `hax-element-schema` (`HAXElementSchema`, the lightweight `{tag, properties, content, eventName}` virtual-DOM object HAX uses for insertion, duplication, and DOM↔schema conversion via `haxElementToNode`/`nodeToHaxElement`; companion to `hax-schema`, since `demoSchema` entries are `HAXElementSchema` objects); `merlin-schema` (the Option/Program contract for Merlin, the universal command palette and voice assistant implemented by `<super-daemon>`, opened with `Alt+Shift` and shared across HAXcms, the HAX body editor, and app-hax); `appstore-spec` (the schema for HAX's media/app browser — external media provider definitions in `apps`, reusable content stacks in `stax`, and preloaded custom elements in `autoloader`, backing `generateAppStore`-style endpoints that feed the HAX editor's media tray). In PRAW RULES.md (scope: global). Guidance by design: no check enforces this, and none is planned. Says which contract repo to read before working against it.

r_mlhl56jnsqhvnriaw5a2gr.desc: The design system called DDD is located under the path `elements/d-d-d` and should be leveraged for fonts, colors, padding, spacing, margins and other consistency in component and site design. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: design-system). Also in webcomponents AGENTS.md. Enforced by DDD token lint.

r_mt6hpj9bdha13jwsxjcmea.desc: Whenever working on a specific webcomponent, perform a quick audit to ensure proper usage of the DDD design system. (Design-system detail lives in `design-system/WARP.md`.) In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Enforced by DDD token lint.

r_k0lv6bjoprqp7ijmzkemuw.desc: We have an older color based designs system called SimpleColors. We still use this in order to fill in gaps in DDD as far as shades of all colors. SimpleColors creates a base line color spectrum for levels of red, orange, blue, etc. When possible we should be using DDD's colors instead of these, though there are elements that will still leverage it in unique situations. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: design-system). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_c4f0b69d_9ed4_4b6d_bf52_6a3d9937c98f.desc: For any design-related decisions in this repository, `DESIGN.md` at the repository root is the canonical source of truth. Future design work must conform to its design tokens, CSS variable implementation patterns, component guidance, and Do's/Don'ts. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: design-system). Guidance by design: no check enforces this, and none is planned. Says which document settles design questions in this repo; a person or agent applies it while designing.

r_447f8d9bc5484749b1188e.desc: Use `data-primary` / `data-accent` for a single color on an element (they set `--ddd-theme-primary` / `--ddd-theme-accent`); use `data-palette` for a coordinated multi-color palette across a region or site (`--ddd-palette-color-1` to `-7`, palettes `0` to `7`). `DDDPaletteStyles` selects `[data-palette="N"]`, not `:host([data-palette])`, so those styles must exist where they can match the element: extend `DDDSuper(...)` so DDD registers at the document level, or add `DDDAllStyles` to the global theme stylesheet via `HAXCMSGlobalStyleSheetContent()`. Shadow-scoped inclusion alone can make palette switching silently do nothing. Details: KNOWLEDGE.md entry "DDD data-palette". In PRAW RULES.md (scope: design-system). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_1992902d74844c908ab446.desc: Admin surfaces (anything only a signed-in editor sees whose job is to change settings or data: site admin and its sections, outline-designer, revisions, reports, system admin, and editor chrome as it is updated) use HAX UI, the admin layer of DDD, not DDD's content scale. Spread `HaxUiAdminTokens` and `HaxUiAdminPrimitives` from `@haxtheweb/hax-body/lib/hax-ui-styles.js` and style with `--hax-ui-*` only (14px text, 32px rows, one accent; every value maps to a DDD primitive). Site and system admin sections render inside the one admin dialog and never draw their own titlebar or Save button: the shell's action bar stages saves, lights Save when there are changes and asks before leaving with unsaved changes. Authored content, themes and anything a visitor sees stay on DDD. Missing values go into `HaxUiAdminTokens` (mapped to DDD) before use; proposed tokens are documentation until adopted. Guide: `elements/d-d-d/design-system/source/hax-ui-admin.md` in haxtheweb/webcomponents; audit with `hax-pattern-library-audit` (`contract-admin-*`). outline-designer is the reference implementation. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: design-system). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_ccca6768_05e0_4d4d_b3a1_4b9895531558.desc: A prototype of HAXcms itself (whole-site designs, the editor top bar and edit mode, menus, outline, site or system admin, the dashboard, and any multipage flow) is built on the running system from latest main, never redrawn from memory. Use the `haxcms-prototype` skill (<https://github.com/haxtheweb/praw/tree/main/skills/haxcms-prototype>). Write the prototype brief first: the real states shown, in order, and exactly what is proposed in each. The base of every state is either a branch of the real code or an unchanged capture from the haxcms-nodejs UI inventory (`npm run ui:inventory`); only the proposed change is authored by hand, and it is always visibly marked as proposed. Visible text outside proposed regions must be real labels; new labels, components and tokens are declared in the brief. Styles come from the inventory's `tokens.css` (HAX UI for admin surfaces and editor chrome, DDD for anything a visitor sees, per `1992902d74844c908ab446`), never retyped values. Multipage and admin flows show each step as its own real state. Every prototype carries its provenance (commit SHAs, inventory date, fixture) and passes the skill's fidelity check before review. When review finds drift, fix the prototype and record the cause: an inventory gap is fixed in `scripts/ui-inventory.js`, a repeatable agent mistake goes in the skill's deviation log. A loose concept sketch is allowed only when asked for, labeled "Concept, not the current UI", and is never reviewed as a HAXcms prototype. Single elements use `hax-element-demo`. Tracked in haxtheweb/issues#3234. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: design-system). Guidance by design: no check enforces this, and none is planned. Says how to build a HAXcms prototype (on the running system, with the haxcms-prototype skill); no check can tell a redrawn prototype from a real one.

r_956c54783626475ea901a6.desc: Every field in admin chrome (app-hax, HAXcms core UI, the editor, outline-designer, the character builder) is a `simple-fields-field`: text, search, select, textarea, checkbox and radio. Style it with `HaxUiAdminSimpleFields` from `@haxtheweb/d-d-d/lib/HaxUiAdminControls.js` (`class="hax-ui-simple-field"`, `compact` for a 32px toolbar field) and read changes from `value-changed` (`e.detail.value`; it also fires for the value it was rendered with, so set state from it rather than toggling). Never hand-draw `<input>`, `<select>` or `<textarea>` in admin chrome: a native control styled per element is how white-on-white dark mode bugs slip through, and one element gives one look, one keyboard and screen reader behavior and one place where light and dark colors are set. Hidden and file inputs are not fields. Enforced in haxtheweb/webcomponents by the HAX UI admin contract check (`yarn lint:hax-ui-admin`, rule `raw-field`), which fails `yarn precheck` and CI on a new hand-drawn field; fields that predate the rule are listed in `scripts/hax-ui-admin-contract.baseline.json` and are converted when their files are touched. Extends `1992902d74844c908ab446`. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: design-system). Enforced by hax-ui-admin-contract. The HAX UI admin contract check (yarn lint:hax-ui-admin, rule raw-field) fails yarn precheck and the pull request on a new hand-drawn field in admin chrome; fields that predate the rule are baselined.

r_411423ec_d922_4bd4_8c45_3d8c65b9fbfa.desc: Every part of HAX that people are shown (a project area, backend, tool, schema, surface or site in the network) has one icon, one DDD color and one icon motion, and all three are on record in PRAW before it ships: the `%%@ node <id> icon=<set:name> color=<DDD color name> motion=<DDD motion name>` line in the ecosystem web that draws it (`ecosystem/web/hax-ecosystem.mmd` for an area, that area's sub-web for a part of it) and, for a site, its entry in `ecosystem/network.json`. That record is the only copy: anything that shows an area (a site, the network bar, a dashboard or Merlin entry, docs, social art, a poster) takes the icon, color and motion from it and never picks its own, and a change is made to the record first. The icon is in `@haxtheweb/simple-icon` or `@haxtheweb/hax-iconset`, drawn in one ink on the 24 grid, and is HAX's own mark: never another project's logo, mascot or wordmark. The color is a DDD named color with a black or white glyph, whichever contrasts more. The motion is one of the nine DDD icon motions (`pop`, `wiggle`, `tilt`, `beat`, `lift`, `spin`, `nudge`, `strike`, `glow`; the scale motion is `beat`, `pulse` is the attention ring), which plays once on hover or keyboard focus, never moves under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and never carries meaning alone. Style guide, when to use each motion and how to add one: `ecosystem/README.md`, "Area icons, colors and motion" (<https://github.com/haxtheweb/praw/blob/main/ecosystem/README.md#area-icons-colors-and-motion>). In PRAW RULES.md (scope: design-system). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_rvsctsdjae8lrmsjmpo3mk.desc: Elements with a haxProperties method are HAX capable, leveraging the HAXSchema standard to interface with the HAX editor. The demoSchema part provides all necessary information to create example elements in HAX. For demos launching in codepen, use demoSchema and HAX helper methods to create valid demos with appropriate tag names, properties, and slotted content for accurate examples. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Also in webcomponents AGENTS.md. Enforced by haxschema. The HAXSchema check fails a webcomponents pull request when a changed element's haxProperties don't validate or don't match what it declares; known problems are baselined and the baseline only shrinks.

r_7cpveferpsf0az8tkqxw0y.desc: Whenever working on a specific webcomponent, perform a quick audit for potential accessibility enhancements without assuming issues exist, but ensure to look for them. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Enforced by Color contrast of changed elements, Test all elements, Accessibility sweep. The color-contrast gate fails a PR when a touched element's demo falls below WCAG AA contrast in light or dark mode; element test suites include axe checks where an element has tests; the weekly sweep checks every demo. Other accessibility checks are not a blocking gate.

r_13a03330_483e_404e_9e48_b0d9f16432d3.desc: Any pair of controls or states a person must tell apart (accept vs dismiss, save vs cancel, keep vs delete, on vs off, pressed vs not pressed) must stay distinguishable in greyscale (low-power and night modes, personal preference) and with red/green or blue/yellow color vision deficiencies. Hue alone never carries the difference: either the two fills differ by at least 3:1 in luminance, or a non-color cue does the work. Use the HAX UI conventions: fill weight shows which action is primary (filled, then outlined, then text); the diagonal hatch (`--hax-ui-danger-hatch`, `--hax-ui-danger-hatch-on-fill`) shows that an action throws work away; pressed and on states add a bar, border or knob position, not only a wash. When you add or change such a pair, declare it in `scripts/vision-pairs.json` in haxtheweb/webcomponents (with `evidence` for any non-color cue, so removing the cue later fails the check) and run `yarn lint:vision`; `yarn precheck` runs it blocking. Judge what the math can't see (icons, patterns, layout) with `yarn vision:gallery <url> --selector <css>`, or DevTools > Rendering > Emulate vision deficiencies. HAX's correct/incorrect convention (purple vs green, not red vs green) follows from the same rule. Tracking: <https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues/issues/3219>. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_8d0c033b_7c96_4c6e_aafc_7dfff8ad9123.desc: Anything that carries meaning a user must interpret, or a decision with consequences (saving permanently, deleting permanently, confirm vs deny, correct vs incorrect), conveys it through all five channels: (1) a label shown on hover and on focus; (2) a color different enough to tell apart (HAX uses green for correct and purple for incorrect, not red); (3) a focus state; (4) a texture or pattern that still distinguishes it in grayscale; (5) an icon unique to that meaning. Applies to: quiz feedback, confirm/deny and accept/cancel actions, form validation, status chips (draft/published/locked), outline states (new/deleting/current page), revision diffs, chart series and learner progress, reading flags and highlights. Easily undone edits (e.g. turning a paragraph into a heading) and purely navigational or aesthetic controls only need a clear label, a focus state and contrast. Does not need texture: ordinary toolbar buttons, navigation links and menus, tabs and toggles (a selected state still needs more than color). This extends the Color Vision rule (`13a03330-483e-404e-9e48-b0d9f16432d3`), whose danger hatch and `yarn lint:vision` pairs cover the color and texture channels. Enforcement: checked in review, and by the accessibility checks where automatable. Tracking: <https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues/issues/3262>. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Enforced by a11y-modes. Partly. The a11y-modes check in webcomponents fails a pull request when a changed element loses its focus indicator or a control disappears under forced colors (the focus channel), and yarn lint:vision in yarn precheck covers the color and texture channels for the pairs declared in scripts/vision-pairs.json. The label and icon channels are checked in review. The standard is written in RULES.md and in the DDD authoring guide (elements/d-d-d/design-system/source/README.md, Meaning channels).

r_34ef39a0_b970_43ba_b68a_251f99d64424.desc: Every element responds to dark mode and respects reduced motion. Colors an element sets change in dark mode: take them from DDD tokens (which have dark values) or switch them with `light-dark()`, `prefers-color-scheme` or `color-scheme`; never hard-code colors that render the same in both schemes. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, no CSS animation, transition or `element.animate()` longer than 10ms runs on the element or in its shadow root, on load or on hover/focus. The webcomponents `dark-motion` check enforces this for every element a pull request changes; its baseline (`scripts/dark-motion.baseline.json`) only shrinks. Contrast in each scheme is the contrast check's job. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Enforced by dark-motion. The dark-motion check opens each changed element's demo in light and dark with reduced motion on, and fails the pull request on a new failure.

r_cehsaztyfb2vtcwthggnbk.desc: When writing global scope referenced JavaScript, use `globalThis` instead of `window` for consistency. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Also in webcomponents AGENTS.md. Enforced by ESLint. ESLint no-restricted-globals (window) in webcomponents: an error in CI (the ESLint step of the build workflow) and in yarn precheck.

r_njf4syugdn5wr5tevadtgy.desc: Do not use the optional chaining syntax (`?.`) because the current toolchain / Polymer parser has issues with this syntax. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Enforced by ESLint. ESLint no-restricted-syntax (ChainExpression) in webcomponents: an error in CI (the ESLint step of the build workflow) and in yarn precheck before push.

r_410c4334_a186_4356_9584_0796e5d2bc2d.desc: An `id` reference (`aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-controls`, `aria-owns`, `aria-activedescendant`, `<label for>`) only resolves inside the tree it is written in. One that points from light DOM into a shadow root, or out of a shadow root to light DOM, finds nothing and fails silently: no error, no axe failure in many cases, just a control with no name. Inside an element, keep the labelling control and its label in the same shadow root, or take the label as a property/attribute and render it next to the control. To label a shadow-internal control from slotted or light DOM content, set the reflected element properties (`ariaLabelledByElements`, `ariaDescribedByElements`, `ariaControlsElements`) in `firstUpdated`/`updated`; they resolve outward only (shadow tree to light DOM or ancestor trees), never inward, so a host cannot be labelled by its own shadow content this way. They are Baseline Newly available, so feature-detect (`'ariaLabelledByElements' in Element.prototype`) and keep a working label when they are missing (see the Browser Support Policy rule `4e0800ef-32ff-42dc-83f0-bbb953d97554`). Focus: when the element wraps one internal focusable control that owns the semantics (an input, a button), attach the shadow root with `delegatesFocus: true` (in Lit, `static shadowRootOptions = { ...LitElement.shadowRootOptions, delegatesFocus: true }`) instead of putting `tabindex` on the host; do not also give the host a role or state, or focus lands on the inner control and the host's state is skipped. When the host itself is the control (a custom toggle with `role` and `aria-pressed` on the host), put `tabindex="0"` on the host and leave `delegatesFocus` off. Never use a positive `tabindex`. Check this when adding or reviewing labels, descriptions or focus handling in an element; `hax-a11y-audit` checks the authored-content side. Source: Modern Web Guidance `accessible-web-components`. Tracking: <https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues/issues/3298>. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_eis0l9w9l2jg1cofysmvdt.desc: When you write content for hax sites make sure that the webcomponent tags you are using are things that could have been authored and put in the page. This means written using the HAX editor via elements that have HAXSchema. This registry has a list of all valid HAX capable elements and while not always used on every page, it's useful for knowing what is possible. Some times supplying visually interesting content helps with engagement for video, table, and block element data. Also keep in mind the DDD attributes that we support to help make headings and paragraph content offset in a consistent way. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_haxhooks_lifecycle_integration.desc: Elements that need to participate in HAX lifecycle / state changes without importing HAX implement a `haxHooks()` method mapping hook names to element method names. r_40983ddf_40b7_4a5e_a600_8f9fcb58da83.desc: Content made with the HAX editor must work when HAX is not present. r_2e0e8483_8e58_4854_b6f9_f28f77aec17b.desc: Tracking stores the smallest record that answers the question being asked (did they go through the page, did they finish the activity), not raw behavior. Once an outcome is complete it stops being recorded, and it never fires twice in one visit. Thresholds forgive (about 80% of checkpoints seen, never pixel-exact). A new statement type names what reads it (a report, a completion rule, the tracked view); if nothing reads it, it is not recorded. Rationale: KNOWLEDGE.md entry "Tracking is translucent: visible to the tracked, abstract by default". In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_6150b048_e030_467c_b1f7_2ceaa271f00e.desc: Every xAPI statement a HAX element sends conforms to xAPI 1.0.3: it validates against the statement schema, scores sit within their min and max, and each `result.response` and `correctResponsesPattern` follows the grammar of its interaction type. r_1b8b8a93_0458_41f9_85a4_ba8d16923765.desc: When creating a new component or theme, or working in an existing one, audit it for server-side rendering (SSR) without assuming issues exist. The server runs only the constructor, `willUpdate` and `render`; `connectedCallback`, `firstUpdated`, `updated` and `disconnectedCallback` do not run. Safety: (1) Keep the constructor, `willUpdate`, `render` and anything they call free of `document.body`, `document.head`, `localStorage` / `sessionStorage`, `location` and layout measurements. The shim supplies an inert `window`, event listeners, `matchMedia`, observers and query / child / class / style APIs, so those do not throw but find nothing, and `getBoundingClientRect` returns zeros. (2) Put browser-only work, including reading storage and measuring layout, in `connectedCallback`, `firstUpdated` or `updated`. (3) Guard any browser API the server can reach with `globalThis` (`typeof globalThis.document !== 'undefined'`, `globalThis.localStorage && ...`) or a try / catch, never a bare `window` / `document` reference, and do not use `?.`. (4) Add listeners and observers in `connectedCallback` and remove them in `disconnectedCallback`, so they keep working if the element is moved. (5) Keep import-time side effects out of helper modules; an element module defining its own tag is expected. (6) Load browser-only dependencies with dynamic `import()` from client-only lifecycle methods. (7) An element that cannot render on the server (WebGL, audio, real layout) sets `static ssr = false`, optionally with `static ssrSkipReason`, instead of throwing. (9) The shim's `children` is empty, so data the first render needs must arrive through properties or attributes, not be read from light DOM children after upgrade; if an element keeps authored data in light DOM, make sure the render is still meaningful without it. (10) In templates, use attribute bindings instead of property bindings on native elements: `?checked` / `?disabled` rather than `.checked` / `.disabled` (SSR writes `.checked=${false}` out as `checked="false"`, which browsers read as on until hydration), and `src=${v}` / `href=${v}` (with `ifDefined` when it can be undefined) rather than `.src` / `.href` (SSR does not write a property binding at all, so an `

r_47905658_f1c9_448d_99e5_9e933bdc6990.desc: An element points the i18n manager at its locales by naming its English locale file and stepping back to the folder: `new URL("./locales/<tag>.en.json", import.meta.url).href + "/../"` (from `lib/`, `../locales/<tag>.en.json`). This applies to `registerLocalization` and to the haxProperties `i18n-manager-register-element` event alike. Never point `new URL()` at the folder (`"./locales/"`, `` `./locales` ``) or at a language file the element does not commit (such as a scaffold's `.ar.json`): bundlers using `@web/rollup-plugin-import-meta-assets` fail on both (EISDIR on 1.x, ENOENT on every version). Name the file literally, never with a runtime expression such as `` `../locales/${this.tag}.es.json` `` (`tag` is static, so on an instance that is `undefined`, and a bundler cannot resolve it). A base element that sites subclass with their own tag passes `namespace: "<tag>"` so the subclass still loads its translations. The `"/../"` resolves back to `locales/`, so the runtime fetch is identical unbundled. Anchor on English because it is the one locale file every element commits (feature PRs are English-only). An element with only haxProperties locales anchors on a haxProperties file it ships. A bundled site still copies element `locales/*.json` next to the emitted anchor asset if it wants languages beyond the anchor. Enforced in haxtheweb/webcomponents by `yarn lint:locale-urls` (blocking in `yarn precheck` and CI). The `hax webcomponent` templates ship `<name>.en.json` and anchor on it. Extends haxtheweb/issues#1616. Tracking: <https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues/issues/3402>. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Enforced by Locale URLs point at a shipped locale file. Partly. Template lint's locale-url check fails the pull request when new URL() for locales names the locales/ folder or a file that doesn't ship; that it is the English file is checked in review.

If a custom config is unavoidable (for example to point at a different browser binary), spread the repo config and override only the launcher. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Guidance by design: no check enforces this, and none is planned. Says which runner config to use when running tests locally.

r_932f6cd4_90a9_451c_98af_4fb577007f9d.desc: Do not wait for asynchronous work in tests (or e2e flows) with a fixed `setTimeout`/sleep. Poll for the condition the test actually needs (a property, attribute, rendered node or dialog) with a bounded timeout, so a slow CI runner passes and a real failure still reports the real assertion. Use fixed waits only to prove that something does not happen. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_4e5b2533_8d87_4d77_b303_2d2907a78339.desc: New or changed code that sanitizes, validates, parses or saves untrusted or bulk input (HTML/URL sanitizers, path and name validators, importers, `saveOutline`-style bulk writes) ships with a fast-check property test next to its example tests. Follow the HAX fuzz convention (<https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues/issues/3272>): read parameters through the repo's `fuzzConfig()` helper (`test/_helpers/fuzz-config.cjs` in `create` and `haxcms-nodejs`, `scripts/test-setup/fuzz-config.mjs` in `webcomponents`) with a fixed `defaultSeed`, never a bare `{ numRuns }` that draws a new random seed on every CI run; name the file `*-fuzz.test.js` so `test:fuzz` hunt mode picks it up (`.js`, not `.cjs`, where the repo allows it, because the OpenSSF Scorecard Fuzzing check only scans `.js`/`.jsx`); and when a hunt finds a failure, fix it and pin the shrunk counterexample as a fast-check `examples` entry or a plain test so the default run guards it. Replay a reported failure with `HAX_FUZZ_SEED=<seed> HAX_FUZZ_PATH=<path>`. Properties state what must always hold ("never throws", "never lets a `javascript:` URL through", "output equals the old implementation"), not one expected output. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: global). Enforced by Fuzz hunt, fuzz-nightly, nightly.

r_35309388_b7be_40ca_88a9_539fe1dd4b0d.desc: When an asynchronous lookup (IndexedDB, fetch, storage) assigns to a component property, check that the property has not been set in the meantime before assigning (compare against the value read when the lookup started, or only assign while it is still unset). Otherwise a late result silently clobbers a user or test action, producing intermittent failures that depend on timing. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_896ecfa1_8965_4c06_a3ab_31c7e7eb28bf.desc: Some elements override `querySelectorAll` (for example `video-player`'s SSR stub, which returns `[]`), so shared helpers that call `el.querySelectorAll(...)` on an arbitrary element can silently do nothing. In shared code call the platform method directly (`Element.prototype.querySelectorAll.call(el, selector)`) or walk `el.children`/`el.childNodes`, and keep SSR stubs inert only for the element's own use. Tests for such helpers must assert that the expected node or object is actually found (and, for removals, that it is gone), not merely that the call did not throw; a failed assertion on a DOM node can also hang the test page until the runner's finish timeout. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Nothing enforces this yet.

r_8e6a9af3_0301_4c48_b75f_fcff2fc928e6.desc: An element that is removed from the page must leave nothing reachable behind; long editing sessions otherwise grow without bound (haxtheweb/issues#3237). Four patterns caused every leak found so far, and each has a fix: (1) MobX `autorun`/`reaction` created in a `constructor` — create it in `connectedCallback`, keep the disposer, dispose it in `disconnectedCallback` (a constructor runs once, so it can neither be disposed when the element never connects nor recreated after a reconnect); (2) a class that fills `this.__disposer` without a `disconnectedCallback` that runs it — add one; (3) a `responsive-utility` registration (`"responsive-element"` event or `registerResponsiveElement()`) without `unregisterResponsiveElement()` on disconnect — its ResizeObserver keeps the element alive; (4) markup parsed in the live document only to be read back (`document.createElement("div").innerHTML = …`, `document.createRange().createContextualFragment()`) — custom elements in it upgrade and register globally; parse in `document.implementation.createHTMLDocument("")` or a `<template>`. The `haxtheweb-leaks/*` ESLint rules flag all four (existing hits are suppressed, so only new code is reported). `yarn test:leaks` (`scripts/leak-check.mjs`) proves it at runtime: it builds each HAX-capable element in the folders you changed from its first `demoSchema` entry, attaches and removes it repeatedly in Chromium, and fails on anything that grows with the cycles (global listeners, observers, timers, animation-frame loops, globalThis stores, uncollected instances) that `scripts/leak-check.baseline.json` does not already list for that tag; `--tags a-b,c-d` or `--all` widen it. When a fix removes an element's leak, refresh its baseline in the same PR (`yarn test:leaks:baseline --tags <tag>`) so the leak can't come back. When a fix removes a lint hit, prune its suppression (`npx eslint <files> --prune-suppressions`): ESLint fails on suppressions that no longer occur. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Enforced by Memory leaks.

r_13166db2_909f_4a34_87d1_1b697834eb4b.desc: Before opening a PR that touches `haxcms-elements` core (store, site builder, router, theme base classes), the site menu, i18n, or a theme, run the haxcms-nodejs perf harness against the monorepo source: `NODE_ENV=development HAXCMS_WEBCOMPONENTS_ROOT=<your webcomponents checkout> npm run perf:memory -- --short` in a haxcms-nodejs checkout (about 90 seconds), once on `master` and once on the branch, and compare the per-visit numbers (heap, DOM nodes, listeners, live MobX reactions, observed detached nodes, i18n registrations). If any moved, put the before/after in the PR. For load-time changes run `npm run perf:lighthouse -- --short`; for changes whose cost grows with page count run `npm run perf:scale -- --sizes 100,500,1000`. Lighthouse alone does not catch memory regressions. See https://github.com/haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs/tree/main/test/perf (haxtheweb/issues#3245). In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Enforced by Render benchmarks. Render benchmarks run on PRs and report without failing.

r_0cf20bb0_0afa_4c6a_9100_e76f76a5cc1a.desc: outline-designer is how bulk structure changes happen; what it shows must be exactly what `saveOutline` stores. r_z61ldoq98dttlrwen7tl9t.desc: Code in a HAXsite's `custom/` folder (custom themes and site-specific elements bundled into `custom/build/custom.es6.js`) builds on the HAXcms base class instead of bare third-party imports. r_92dfb3b2_1c32_42dc_89c3_0f4ae66f7227.desc: User prefers to always use the latest Node.js LTS release across the ecosystem (currently Node 24). r_4e0800ef_32ff_42dc_83f0_bbb953d97554.desc: HAX supports the current and previous release of each evergreen browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari). In Baseline terms: **Widely available** features are used freely; **Newly available** features are allowed behind feature detection (`'x' in obj`, `CSS.supports()`, `@supports`) with a plainer path that still works without them; **Limited availability** needs a reason in the PR plus the same detection. No polyfills, and no dependency added only to fake a platform feature. This replaces Modern Web Guidance's default, which treats only Widely available as safe and adds fallbacks for the rest. Repos state it in `AGENTS.md` as: `**Browser Support:** Current and previous evergreen browsers. Baseline Widely available features without fallbacks; Baseline Newly available features behind feature detection with a working plain path; no polyfills.` The `baseline-js` lint is the PR-time check. Tracking: <https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues/issues/3298>. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: webcomponents). Enforced by ESLint. ESLint baseline-js/use-baseline in webcomponents flags JavaScript features that are not Baseline Widely available unless the line says why; an error in CI and in yarn precheck. r_f54de8cb_0b65_4f50_98e6_43e8c2ebc4c7.desc: Modern Web Guidance (MWG) and other outside agent guidance are advice; where they conflict with a HAX rule, the HAX rule wins and the PR says which advice was set aside. r_186fad44_1725_470e_80a7_903ea54fce1a.desc: Before editing in a repo, read its `AGENTS.md` and the `scripts` in its `package.json` to find the lint, format and test commands it expects; do not assume a check you ran elsewhere is the one it uses. Before pushing code or opening a PR, run the repo's `precheck` script (`npm run precheck`; `yarn precheck` in `webcomponents`), fix every failure it reports, and re-run until it passes (`precheck:fix` repairs formatting and fixable lint). Run it again after your last commit, not only after the first. Repos with a `precheck` script (`create`, `haxcms-nodejs`, `webcomponents`) also block `git push` and `gh pr create` via a Claude Code hook, but that hook only fires for those commands, run from inside that repo; a PR opened another way (for example `gh api` where GraphQL is unavailable) or from another working directory is not checked, so run `precheck` yourself first. Do not bypass it by loosening lint or format configs, adding ignore entries, or skipping hooks. ESLint alone is not a substitute: it commonly ignores test files, which Prettier still checks, so a new test file can pass lint and fail format. In a repo without `precheck` (for example `haxcms-php`), run its test suite and any lint or format-check scripts it has on the files you changed, and say in the PR description what you ran. In a sparse or partial checkout where `precheck` or its config is missing, run Prettier and ESLint directly with the repo's own config on the changed files, and say what could not be run. After pushing, check the PR's CI results (`gh pr checks`, or the REST API where GraphQL is unavailable) and, if a check fails, read its logs, fix the cause, and push again. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: global). Guidance by design: no check enforces this, and none is planned. Says what an agent does before submitting (read AGENTS.md, run the repo's own lint and tests); the checks it points to are each enforced on their own.

r_cd0800bf_8611_4835_a421_ad10e88b01e9.desc: A PR must pass the CodeQL check on its first push; do not leave security alerts for the reviewer to send back. Before pushing, run CodeQL locally on what you changed with the same query suite and `paths-ignore` the repo's CodeQL workflow uses. In `webcomponents` this is part of `yarn precheck` (`yarn codeql` on its own); install the CLI once per session with `yarn codeql:install`, and the Claude Code push hook blocks `git push` and `gh pr create` until the scan is clean. In a repo without that script, download the official CodeQL bundle (<https://github.com/github/codeql-action/releases>), create a JavaScript database scoped to the changed folders using the repo's `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml`, analyze with `codeql/javascript-queries:codeql-suites/javascript-code-scanning.qls`, and fix every alert that lands in a changed file; the reference implementation is <https://github.com/haxtheweb/webcomponents/blob/master/scripts/codeql-local.mjs>. Fix alerts in the code, never by suppressing them, loosening the CodeQL config or adding `paths-ignore` entries. Recurring HAX alerts to avoid while writing: `Math.random()` for ids or anything that reaches the DOM (use a counter or `crypto.randomUUID()`), single-pass or case-sensitive tag/HTML sanitization and quadratic regexes (use linear-time patterns, repeat until stable, or a real parser), assigning to object keys taken from input without guarding `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype`, and turning DOM text back into HTML. Say in the PR description that the local CodeQL scan ran and its result. In PRAW RULES.md (scope: global). Enforced by CodeQL.

r_5cf2787e_c2df_4184_8b61_53c42ffad9cf.desc: In AI-assisted output, dates, points, counts, ids, slugs and outline order are inserted by code from the source data; the model only writes the prose around them. r_9b2e454c_9b5b_46dc_b443_6470b3b4abe9.desc: A prompt is fitted to the model's context and output limits before the call, and anything left out is stated to the person; content is never cut to fit without saying so. rc_content_contract.desc: Attributes, usage and existing labels of authorable elements never change, so all content ever made keeps working. Visual and language-support improvements are fine. Proposed in the HAX Scheduled Background Jobs Plan; now written into PRAW RULES.md as part of "HAX Rules Win Over Modern Web Guidance". Enforced by Element API snapshot.

rc_user_links.desc: Links an author writes (http included) are kept as written. Proposed in the HAX Scheduled Background Jobs Plan; now written into PRAW RULES.md as part of "HAX Rules Win Over Modern Web Guidance". Nothing enforces this yet.

rc_version_hidden.desc: No version number reaches anyone who isn't logged in. Proposed in the HAX Scheduled Background Jobs Plan; not written into RULES.md or AGENTS.md yet. Enforced by Unit and API conformance tests, PHPUnit. haxcms-nodejs test/unit/version-not-exposed-unauthenticated.test.cjs runs in its unit tests; haxcms-php OpenApiRouteContractTest::testVersionAndStatusEndpointsAreNeverPublic runs in PHPUnit. Both fail the pull request.

rc_no_native_dialogs.desc: Confirmation steps are built into the page, never the browser's prompt(), confirm() or alert(). Proposed in the HAX Scheduled Background Jobs Plan; now written into PRAW RULES.md as part of "HAX Rules Win Over Modern Web Guidance". Enforced by ESLint. ESLint no-alert (alert, confirm and prompt calls) in webcomponents, an error in CI and in yarn precheck (haxtheweb/issues#3295).

rc_explicit_js.desc: Our own elements are imported with the full .js file path, since the server can't load extensionless paths. Proposed in the HAX Scheduled Background Jobs Plan; now written into PRAW RULES.md as part of "HAX Rules Win Over Modern Web Guidance". Enforced by ESLint. ESLint no-restricted-syntax in webcomponents flags extensionless or bare imports of @haxtheweb/* and relative modules; an error in CI and in yarn precheck.

rc_ddd_layers.desc: Each surface uses its DDD layer: content scale for what readers see, the denser HAX UI style for admin surfaces, and the instructional element blueprint for activities. Proposed in the HAX Scheduled Background Jobs Plan; not written into RULES.md or AGENTS.md yet. Nothing enforces this yet.

rc_correct_colors.desc: Correct is green and incorrect is purple, never red, for decisions with consequences. Proposed in the HAX Scheduled Background Jobs Plan; now written into PRAW RULES.md as part of "Meaning Channels — Meaning and Consequential Decisions Use All Five". Nothing enforces this yet.
